- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.27 for 2+ days), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility >0.3.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment >0.27 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly negative and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1% to forecast for next 5 days.
